word.definitionEN: a firm belief, or the act of being found guilty of a crime
examples: He spoke with conviction about the importance of honesty.
Her conviction that education can change lives inspired many people in the community.

word.definitionEN: the quality of being able to compete successfully with others
examples: Their competitiveness helps them succeed in business.
The country's competitiveness in the global economy depends on factors such as innovation, education, and infrastructure.

word.definitionEN: letters sent or received; a close similarity or connection
examples: She keeps all her old correspondence in a box.
They maintained regular correspondence during the war.
There is a clear correspondence between the two sets of data, indicating a strong correlation.

word.definitionEN: to hold or include something within itself
examples: The box contains old photographs.
The report contains detailed information about the project.

word.definitionEN: to quote or refer to something as evidence or example
examples: She cited a famous quote in her speech.
The professor asked the students to cite their sources in the research paper.
The lawyer cited a previous court ruling to strengthen her argument in the case.

word.definitionCN: 表達、傳達（思想、感情或想法）
word.definitionEN: to communicate or make known an idea or feeling
examples: The report conveys important information about the project.
He effectively conveyed his ideas during the meeting.
Please convey the instructions to the team as soon as possible.

word.definitionEN: to make something clearer or easier to understand
examples: Please clarify the terms of the agreement before we proceed.
The manager will clarify any questions about the new policy in the meeting.

word.definitionEN: overcrowding that causes blockage or slow movement
examples: The city is implementing new measures to reduce traffic congestion.
High network congestion during peak hours can affect internet speeds.
To address congestion problems, the company is upgrading its infrastructure.

word.definitionCN: 至關重要的、關鍵的、決定性的
word.definitionEN: extremely important or necessary
examples: Her work has been crucial to the project's success.

word.definitionCN: 連續的、連貫的、無間斷的
word.definitionEN: following one after another without interruption
examples: This is the fifth consecutive weekend that I've spent working.

word.definitionEN: a group of things sharing common characteristics
examples: The company launched a new product in the electronics category.
They are analyzing the expenses in different categories to reduce costs.

word.definitionEN: a group of people appointed to perform a particular function
examples: Each member of the finance committee is considered an expert in his or her field.

word.definitionEN: to organize and carry out a particular activity
examples: The company will conduct a survey to gather customer feedback.
He is responsible for conducting the meeting this afternoon.

word.definitionCN: 餐飲供應商或外燴業者
word.definitionEN: a person or company that provides food for events
examples: We hired a caterer for the office party.
The caterer provided a variety of food options for the conference.

word.definitionEN: a container holding ink, toner, or other material for a device
examples: The printer needs a new ink cartridge.
They ran out of toner cartridges in the office.

word.definitionEN: the money used in a particular country
examples: Currency fluctuations can impact international trade.
Make sure to check the currency exchange rate before traveling.

word.definitionEN: corresponding in size or degree to something else
examples: His new role comes with a salary commensurate with his skills.
The compensation was not commensurate with the amount of work required.

word.definitionEN: able to exist or work together without conflict
examples: This charger is compatible with most smartphones.
The new system is fully compatible with older versions of the software.

word.definitionEN: a person or company that undertakes work for others
examples: The contractor completed the renovation on time.
They hired a contractor to manage the installation of new equipment.

word.definitionCN: 坐墊、靠墊、緩衝、減少影響
word.definitionEN: a soft pad used for sitting or leaning on, or something that softens an impact
examples: A cushion was added to each chair to improve comfort.
They have a financial cushion to handle unexpected expenses.

word.definitionEN: a formal event held to mark an occasion
examples: The company hosted an award ceremony to honor high-performing employees.

word.definitionEN: an asset offered as security for a loan
examples: To secure the loan, the borrower must provide collateral such as real estate or vehicles.
The bank assessed the collateral value before approving the loan application.

word.definitionEN: holding traditional values and resistant to change
examples: Older people tend to be more conservative and a bit suspicious of anything new.

word.definitionEN: to state something as true, or to formally request something owed
examples: You need to fill out a claim form to receive your refund.
The company denied his claim for damages.

word.definitionEN: to compete for something, or to assert as true
examples: The athlete will contend for the championship title this year.
Many experts contend that the new policy will improve productivity.

word.definitionEN: a long passage in a building connecting rooms
examples: Please follow the corridor to reach the meeting room.
The new office space includes a wide corridor for easy access.

word.definitionEN: a mutual relationship between two or more things
examples: There's a correlation between smoking and cancer.

word.definitionCN: 文書工作的、辦公室工作的
word.definitionEN: relating to office work such as filing and typing
examples: The job requires strong clerical skills and attention to detail.
She applied for a clerical position at the local bank.

word.definitionEN: to act in accordance with a rule or request
examples: All employees must comply with the company's dress code.
The contractor was asked to comply with environmental regulations.

word.definitionEN: to stop doing something or to come to an end
examples: The factory will cease operations at the end of the month.
The company decided to cease production of the outdated model.

word.definitionEN: a large open area in a public building where people gather
examples: The passengers gathered in the airport concourse before boarding.

word.definitionEN: to persuade someone through flattery or gentle urging
examples: The sales manager tried to cajole the client into signing the contract by highlighting all the benefits.

word.definitionCN: 會議結束、表示結束某事或做出判斷或決定
word.definitionEN: to bring something to an end, or to decide something after consideration
examples: After analyzing the data, the team concluded that the project was feasible.

word.definitionEN: a limitation or restriction on action
examples: Due to time constraints, we had to complete the report earlier than expected.
The company operates within strict regulatory constraints to ensure compliance.

word.definitionEN: to begin or start
examples: The project will commence next month after all approvals are finalized.

word.definitionEN: to praise formally or officially
examples: The manager commended the team for their hard work on the project.

word.definitionEN: the extent to which something is reported or included
examples: The media coverage of the event was extensive, reaching millions of viewers.
The company offers health coverage to all its employees.

word.definitionEN: a person or company that delivers messages or packages
examples: I want to have this package delivered by motorcycle courier.

word.definitionEN: a public festival with parades and entertainment
examples: The city organized a carnival to celebrate the holiday season.

word.definitionEN: a standard used to judge or decide something
examples: The primary criterion for the promotion is performance rather than seniority.

word.definitionCN: 忠誠的、堅定的、投入的、全心投入的、承諾的
word.definitionEN: dedicated to a cause, activity, or relationship
examples: The company is committed to providing high-quality services to its clients.

word.definitionCN: 有能力的、能幹的、稱職的
word.definitionEN: having the necessary skill or ability to do something well
examples: She is a competent manager who handles her team effectively.

word.definitionCN: 碰撞：兩個或多個物體相撞的行為
word.definitionEN: an instance of two or more things crashing into each other
examples: The two vehicles were involved in a head-on collision due to slippery roads.

word.definitionCN: 友好而莊重地、熱誠但禮貌地
word.definitionEN: in a warm and friendly but polite manner
examples: We cordially invite you to attend the annual conference next month.

word.definitionEN: causing disagreement or dispute
examples: She avoided answering the controversial question directly.

word.definitionCN: （廣播或電視所播事件的）評論、解說、實況報道
word.definitionEN: a spoken or written description of events as they happen
examples: The sports commentator gave live commentary during the game.

word.definitionCN: 做（違法或錯誤的事）、犯罪、錯、承諾、投入
word.definitionEN: to carry out an act, or to pledge oneself to something
examples: He decided to commit to his job and give it his full attention.

word.definitionEN: to make something stronger or combine into a single whole
examples: He worked hard to consolidate his reputation in the industry.

word.definitionEN: to prepare land for crops, or to develop a skill or relationship
examples: The company aims to cultivate strong relationships with its clients.

word.definitionEN: done or shared by all members of a group
examples: The team's collective effort resulted in the successful launch of the product.

word.definitionEN: rough in texture, or crude in manner
examples: The fabric feels coarse and uncomfortable against the skin.

word.definitionCN: 有能力的、熟練的、能幹的
word.definitionEN: having the ability or skill to do something
examples: The manager capably handled the customer complaints, resolving them quickly.

word.definitionEN: to make something impure or harmful by adding a polluting substance
examples: The food was contaminated by bacteria due to improper storage.

word.definitionEN: skilled work, especially making things by hand
examples: The craftsman demonstrated his skill in creating intricate designs.

word.definitionEN: a room below ground level used for storage
examples: They keep their wine collection in the cellar.

word.definitionCN: 謹慎的、細心的、小心翼翼的
word.definitionEN: careful to avoid risk or danger
examples: He's a cautious driver.

word.definitionCN: 提供飲食、迎合、滿足（需求或喜好）
word.definitionEN: to provide food and service, or to meet someone's needs
examples: They decided to cater the conference to make sure everyone was well-fed.

word.definitionEN: to discuss something with others, or to grant a title or honor
examples: The president will confer with senior advisors before announcing the new policy.

word.definitionEN: the state of being charmed or fascinated
examples: The advertisement had a strong captivation effect on younger audiences.

word.definitionEN: to assert the opposite of a statement, or to be inconsistent with
examples: His actions contradict his earlier promises.

word.definitionEN: relating to mental processes of perception and understanding
examples: The training program helps improve the cognitive skills of employees.
The app is easy to use and reduces the cognitive load on users.
